issue.title: Pager title-chip age reads the wall clock, so 18 pinned time-band PNG goldens drift daily

task_type_fields.why_not_flake: Deterministic: all 18 time-band params (16 test_time_band_png_snapshot params plus 2 test_time_band_narrow_png_snapshot_with_trail params) fail on every run at master ba91bf93c1. The only diff is the title-row relative-age label: the golden says 9d and the render now says 10d (about 293 px). Root cause: src/sase/pager/_screen_chrome.py:72 computes the title chip age with format_age(int(_time.time()), moment.committed_time), from 45ece4f1d00 on 2026-10-01. That ignores the screen's pinned _time_band_now_epoch, which the time band itself honors (src/sase/pager/_screen_time_band.py:84/94) and which the test pins to _NOW = 1790769600 (tests/pager/visual/test_time_band_png_snapshots.py:37,330). The goldens were last regenerated by 1bf61c96f8 on 2026-10-02 against the wall clock. Fix: have the title chip use the pinned epoch when set (falling back to time.time()), then regenerate the time-band goldens with just fix-tui-screenshots, which should yield an age derived from _NOW.

issue.creation_reason: Found by sase-1eu.land while checking epic sase-1eu's pager goldens: every time-band golden now fails on master because the title age moved from 9d to 10d, and no bead tracks it.

payload.description: sibling defect: display sites reading the process clock instead of an injectable now

Phase notes sase-1es.6 #2/#5 and sase-1es.7 #1 saw the same 18 drift identically on clean HEAD. Relayed from epic sase-1es follow-up triage.
